canonical_name: Gershgorin eigenvalue localization theorem family for finite square matrices
literal_source_claim_zh: 矩阵特征值的定位定理
literal_source_claim_en: A localization theorem for matrix eigenvalues.
source_attribution: Semyon Gershgorin, 1931 (catalog metadata; exact primary source not yet admitted)
statement_blocker: The catalog identifies only a matrix-eigenvalue-localization family. It does not select the basic union-of-row-discs inclusion or the stronger disconnected-component eigenvalue-counting result; fix complex versus generalized normed-field scalars; choose finite index and nonempty/dimension conventions; choose row or column discs; define eigenvalues, disc membership, radius, multiplicity, ordered binders, and boundary cases; or provide an admitted primary-source crosswalk. Selecting the pinned candidate as canonical at intake would silently add or omit proposition-changing clauses.
domain_and_universes: Open: an admitted source must select complex n-by-n matrices with an explicit positive dimension or justify the pinned generalization to Matrix n n K for an arbitrary finite index type n and NormedField K; universe and instance choices remain open.
conclusion: Open: likely every eigenvalue lies in at least one closed row disc centered at a diagonal entry with off-diagonal row-norm sum as radius; the catalog does not rule out the stronger separated-component eigenvalue-counting conclusion.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before root selection; empty, zero- and one-dimensional, zero/scalar/diagonal/defective, zero-radius, repeated-eigenvalue, overlapping-disc, disjoint-component, and boundary-membership cases all require source-mapped decisions.

one dimension and zero off-diagonal radius

Brauer Cassini-oval localization, Schur decomposition, the spectral theorem, or Perron-Frobenius
